model: Regulated-utility dividend discount at cost of equity (engine route)

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Management long-term EPS/DPS growth target 7-9% (midpoint 8%, haircut to 7.5% for 1.3%/yr equity dilution and the Illinois ALJ 9.67% ROE signal); cross-checked to the EPS 5-year CAGR of 7.8% (FY2020 3.91 -> FY2025 5.69) and FY2025 adj 5.64 -> FY2027 guide 6.58 = +8.0%/yr.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-yr CAGR 10.9% exceeds EPS 5-yr CAGR 7.8% by ~40%: book equity is inflated by external equity issuance (12.65M shares / $1.69B in 2023; forward-sale settlements 2026), not by organic compounding. Equity CAGR is NOT used as the growth driver.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF (reported FCF - SBC - interest income) is negative in every year: FY2020 -417, FY2021 -344, FY2022 -1,269, FY2023 -799, FY2024 -941, FY2025 -1,189. A CAGR on a negative series is undefined, hence null. The deficit is the rate-base growth programme (capex 2.0x D&A in FY2025 and ~3.5x in FY2025 terms of OCF shortfall), funded by debt and equity -- normal for the sector, not a distress signal. Revenue 3-yr CAGR (10.8%) is flattered by the 2023-2025 rate-case cycle (Pennsylvania, Missouri, Illinois, California) and FY2024 favourable weather; the 5-yr 6.5% is the better through-cycle guide. Dividends paid: FY2021 428, FY2022 467, FY2023 532, FY2024 585, FY2025 633 (+10.3%/yr aggregate; DPS +8%/yr).

scenario_narratives.base: Standalone AWK executes the $48B+ 2026-2035 plan: rate base grows 8-9%, revenue 7-7.5% through FY2031 fading to 5% by FY2035; allowed ROEs stay in the 9.6-10.2% band; adjusted net income margin edges from 22.3% (FY2026 guide) to 23.0% as rate cases recover embedded debt cost; 57.5% payout; 1.3%/yr equity issuance funds the capex-over-OCF gap. Per-share EPS/DPS growth ~7-7.5%, the low-middle of the 7-9% target. Essential merger neutral to per-share value and not in the flows. Value = PV of dividends at an 8.0% CAPM cost of equity plus a Gordon terminal at 3.0% (20.6x dividends, ~12x P/E).
scenario_narratives.bull: Revenue at the top of the rate-base range (8-8.5%), ROEs at or above 10% in Pennsylvania/New Jersey, Essential closes end-Q1 2027 with the promised scale and synergy benefits lifting margin ~1pp, terminal growth 3.5%; EPS growth at the top of the 7-9% band.
scenario_narratives.bear: ROE compression toward 9.5% across the big four states, widening regulatory lag on 5.5%+ debt, PFAS opex and Monterey disallowances, slower acquisition pipeline, merger integration drag; EPS growth ~5%, payout stretched to 60%, terminal 2.5%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A regulated water utility is a bond-like claim on allowed-ROE x rate base. We value the dividend stream at a CAPM cost of equity built from today's 4.86% 10-year yield, not at the ~6.3-6.5% the market's bond-proxy multiple implies, and we do not credit growth capex with value beyond the dividends it ultimately funds. That makes the house number structurally lower than the market's for this sector; the required-return table shows what discount rate today's price implies. Debt is never deducted from an equity flow.
key_risks_to_valuation: Discount rate: every 50bp on the cost of equity moves the base value ~10-12%; the market prices AWK at ~6.3-6.5% versus the 8.0% used here.
Allowed-ROE outcomes in Pennsylvania (24% of regulated revenue), New Jersey (23%), Missouri and Illinois -- the Illinois ALJ's 9.67% recommendation (final order due 2026-12-18) is the near-term test.
Equity issuance pace: the model dilutes 1.3%/yr; the 2023-2026 run-rate was 2.4%/yr including the block raise.

Essential Utilities merger (0.305x, all-stock, end-Q1 2027): close/no-close is roughly value-neutral per share on announcement multiples, but conditions imposed by Pennsylvania/North Carolina/Texas or integration slippage would push toward the bear path.
PFAS: ~$2B compliance capex is rate-base positive, but CERCLA passive-receiver liability is legally unresolved and ~$50M/yr opex arrives from 2029.
Cal Am Monterey Peninsula Water Supply Project ($825M vs $279M approved) and the pending eminent-domain action: disallowance risk on ~8% of regulated revenue.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular close); 52-week range 120.57-153.69.
data_sources.financials: research/AWK/Reports/AWK_Metrics.csv (FY2008-FY2025 annual, quarterlies through Q3 2026); AWK 10-K FY2025 (AWK_Annual_FY2025.txt: adjusted-EPS reconciliation line 5110-5125, forward sale agreements 5539-5540, rate-case ROEs 5224-5249, SBC 6938); AWK 10-Q Q3 2026 (AWK_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt: cover shares 1759, balance sheet 1925-1964, debt table 3188, forward-sale settlement 3681, HOS note repayment 3444, interest income 2002); 10-year UST from Yahoo ^TNX.
data_sources.qualitative: research/AWK/Reports/AWK_Analysis.json (2026-11-08): guidance FY2026 adj EPS $6.07-6.12, FY2027 standalone $6.53-6.63, 7-9% EPS/DPS and 8-9% rate-base targets, capex $3.7B/$4.1B/$20B+/$48B+, Essential merger status, PFAS and Monterey items.

inputs.share_count_basis: 199.105M common shares outstanding at 2026-10-19 (Q3 2026 10-Q cover) plus 4.695M shares still to be physically settled under the August 2025 Forward Sale Agreements by 2026-12-31 (8,098,592 agreed less 3,403,756 settled June 2026) = 203.8M. Then +1.3%/yr: genuine NON-SBC issuance (forward sales, ATM/block equity, stock-funded system acquisitions such as Gordon's Corner) that management states will fund the capex-over-OCF gap for the next five years. SBC is already expensed inside net income and is NOT charged again here. Historical count 182M (FY2022) -> 199M (Q3 2026) = +2.4%/yr including the 2023 $1.69B raise; 1.3% assumes the equity component slows as retained earnings grow. ENGINE CAVEAT: the engine divides the whole equity value by the YEAR-10 count (231.9M), so the near-term dividends (about a third of value) are spread over ~10% more shares than will actually receive them -- a ~2-3% understatement of per-share value, accepted as conservative.
inputs.net_debt_note: Held at ZERO deliberately. The stream being capitalised is a post-interest equity flow (dividends = adjusted net income x payout); debt service is already inside net income and is recovered through rates, so deducting debt again would double-count it (SKILL.md: never FCF/WACC on a post-interest flow, never subtract net debt afterwards). Actual balance sheet at 2026-09-30: long-term debt incl. current portion 14,885 + short-term debt 1,449 = 16,334 total debt; cash 121; net debt 16,213 (D/E 1.37x on 11,931 equity).
inputs.sbc_source: 10-K FY2025 cash flow statement, 'Stock-based compensation 32' (AWK_Annual_FY2025.txt:6938); no separate equity-award tax line disclosed since FY2022, so the add-back is used unadjusted. SBC is a cost already inside net income; sbc_pct_path is 0 in every scenario because the flow capitalised is post-SBC earnings.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2025 interest income of 90 was almost entirely the 10% coupon on the $795M HOS secured seller promissory note, which was repaid in full in February 2026 (Q3 2026 10-Q). It is excluded from the adjusted-EPS base used here and there is no matching asset left to bridge. 9M-2026 interest income was 18 and is running at ~5/yr.
inputs.buyback_note: No repurchases since FY2019; the company is a net ISSUER of equity (forward sales, 2023 block). Share count is therefore grown, not held flat.
inputs.horizon_note: Y1 = FY2026 ... Y10 = FY2035, matching the company's 10-year $48B+ standalone capital plan (2026-2035).
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-06T21:00:02Z regular close (Friday); not an after-hours print
inputs.share_count_date: 2026-10-19 (10-Q cover) plus committed forward-sale shares settling by 2026-12-31
inputs.wacc_rationale: Discount rate is a COST OF EQUITY, not a WACC, because the flow is to equity holders. CAPM built in USD, the flows' own currency: 10-year UST 4.86% (Yahoo ^TNX, 2026-11-06 close) + beta 0.65 (regulated water utility, 5-year range 0.6-0.7) x ERP 4.75% = 7.95%, rounded to 8.0%. Cross-checks: recent authorised ROEs are 9.60-9.84% (Iowa, Kentucky, Tennessee, Virginia, Illinois) with 10.20% in California and the Illinois ALJ proposing 9.67% in October 2026 -- regulators set allowed ROE ~170bp above a CAPM cost of equity, which is the spread that justifies a P/B above 1.0. The market price implies ~6.3-6.5% (bond-proxy premium). Held identical across scenarios: risk is carried in the driver paths and the weights, not in the rate (charge risk once).
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases are immaterial for a water utility (ROU assets are a rounding item against $30B+ utility plant) and lease cost sits inside O&M, hence inside the net income being capitalised. No lease adjustment.
inputs.nci_treatment: No material non-controlling interests; net income attributable to shareholders is the base.
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE. AWK is a rate-regulated water/wastewater utility holding company whose economics are allowed-ROE x rate base. Reported free cash flow is structurally negative in every one of the last 15 years (FY2025 OCF 2,059 vs capex 3,126; FY2026 capex guided $3.7B, FY2027 $4.1B, $20B+ 2026-2030, $48B+ 2026-2035) because growth capex earning ~9.7% allowed ROE exceeds operating cash flow by design and is funded with debt and equity. An unlevered owner-FCF DCF therefore discounts ten years of negative FCF and capitalises a terminal-year FCF that is still negative or near zero -- the AIA.NZ precedent (IV NZ$1.90 vs price NZ$8.76) shows it yields a meaningless number for a capex-supercycle infrastructure asset, and SKILL.md says not to read structurally negative FCF as a signal. The routing table has no utility row; the closest fit is the 'compounder-of-book' family (earnings = allowed ROE x book-like rate base). The flow capitalised is DIVIDENDS = adjusted net income x payout, discounted at a CAPM cost of equity with net debt held at zero, run through the Drivers engine with this mapping: 'revenue' = reported operating revenue (grows with rate base); 'ebitda_margin_path' = ADJUSTED NET INCOME margin (post-interest, post-tax, post-SBC; adjusted EPS basis excludes HOS seller-note interest, weather and Essential transaction costs); 'capex_pct_path' = RETAINED EARNINGS reinvested in rate base (= NI margin x (1 - payout), payout 57.5% base per the ~55-60% policy; FY2026 DPS 3.5125 / EPS guide 6.10 = 57.6%); sbc, D&A, cash tax and working capital paths are 0 because they are already inside net income. FCF line = aggregate dividends; per-share value = PV(dividends) + PV(Gordon terminal on dividends) over a share count that grows 1.3%/yr for equity issuance. Terminal cap 26x dividends = ~15x P/E at 57.5% payout; it is set so the Gordon value (20.6x dividends at 8.0%/3.0%) binds in the base case rather than the cap. ESSENTIAL UTILITIES MERGER: all-stock, 0.305 AWK shares per WTRG share, announced 2025-10-26, targeted close end-Q1 2027; HSR cleared 2026-08-14, Kentucky/Ohio/Virginia approved, Pennsylvania/North Carolina/Texas settlements await ratification. Valued STANDALONE: there is no cash premium to AWK holders, management says the 7-9% EPS/DPS and 8-9% rate-base targets hold post-close, and a stock-for-stock merger at roughly matching multiples is close to value-neutral per AWK share. It is carried as a qualitative item (bull: scale and synergies; bear: integration cost, Pennsylvania politics, 'Burdensome Effect' conditions) rather than built into the flows. Tax: cash taxes are minimal (bonus depreciation, repairs deduction; FY2025 190 incl. CAMT later reversed) and the GAAP effective rate ~22% is already inside net income; CAMT was resolved in AWK's favour by IRS Notice 2026-7.

bear.narrative: Allowed ROEs ratchet down toward 9.5% (the Illinois ALJ's 9.67% becomes the pattern), regulatory lag widens as 5.25-5.70% debt replaces sub-3% vintages, PFAS opex (~$50M/yr from 2029) and Monterey ($825M project, partial disallowance) leak into the margin, and Essential integration costs/conditions dilute. Revenue growth 5.5-6% mid-period, NI margin drifts to 21.5%, payout rises to 60% as the dividend is held while EPS lags (capex_pct = margin x 40%); terminal 2.5%. EPS growth ~5%, below the 7% floor of guidance.

base.growth_rates_note: FY2026 +5.2% (9M-2026 revenue 4,055 vs 3,860 = +5.1%); FY2027 +9.5% as the Pennsylvania ($169M requested), New Jersey ($146M), Illinois ($119M step 1), West Virginia and Virginia rate cases land plus a full year of Nexus; then 7-7.5% tracking the 8-9% rate-base growth target less modest revenue lag, fading to 5% by FY2035 as the plan matures.
base.ebitda_margin_note: This is the ADJUSTED NET INCOME margin, not EBITDA. FY2025 adjusted 21.5% (EPS 5.64 x 195.3M / 5,121); FY2026 22.3% ties to the $6.07-6.12 guide (6.10 x ~197M weighted diluted = 1,201 on 5,387 revenue); FY2027 22.7% on 5,899 revenue = 1,339 = $6.49 on 206.4M shares vs the $6.53-6.63 standalone guide (1-2% below, the dilution-timing haircut). Creeps to 23.0% as rate cases catch up embedded debt cost; held there because 5.25-5.70% refinancing coupons offset operating leverage.
base.capex_pct_note: This is RETAINED EARNINGS reinvested in rate base = NI margin x 42.5% (payout 57.5%). FCF line = dividends = 12.8% of revenue in FY2026 (691 aggregate; 3.39/share on 203.8M vs 3.51 actual DPS, the difference being the year-end vs weighted count).
base.terminal_note: Terminal g 3.0% per share after FY2035, when the 10-year plan ends and rate-base growth should fall toward inflation plus population. Gordon multiple 1.03/(0.08-0.03) = 20.6x dividends = 11.8x P/E -- it binds; the 26x cap (15x P/E) does not.

bull.narrative: Revenue tracks the top of the 8-9% rate-base range, allowed ROEs hold at or above 10% (Pennsylvania 10.95% and New Jersey 10.75% requests largely granted), Essential closes on schedule and synergies lift the net income margin ~1pp above base; payout steady at 57.5%; terminal 3.5%. EPS growth lands at the top of the 7-9% band.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 26x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: 25/50/25 rather than the 15/50/35 house default. A regulated monopoly has a narrow, roughly symmetric outcome distribution: the upside is capped by allowed ROE and the downside is bounded by cost-of-service recovery, so neither tail deserves extra weight. Bull is cut from 35% because it needs two independent things -- constructive ROE orders in Pennsylvania/New Jersey AND a clean Essential close with synergies -- to both go right; bear is lifted from 15% because the rates/ROE-compression path (Illinois ALJ 9.67%, refinancing at 5.25-5.70%) is live evidence, not a hypothetical, and the merger adds political and integration risk through 2027.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
